en: Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Exhortation 22.
The Training Rule on the Setting of the Sun.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the elder bhikkhus were exhorting the bhikkhunīs in turn. On that occasion, it was the turn of the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka to exhort the bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs said, “Today the exhortation will not be successful; the noble Cūḷapanthaka will simply repeat that same inspired utterance over and over again.”
Then those bhikkhunīs approached the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, they sat down to one side.
As they were sitting there, the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka said this to those bhikkhunīs: "Are you in harmony, sisters?
"We are in harmony, venerable sir."
“Sisters, the eight weighty rules (garudhamma) are being observed,” [he asked].
“They are being observed, Noble One,” [they replied].
Having handed over this exhortation (ovāda), saying, “This, sisters, is the instruction,” he uttered this inspired utterance (udāna) again and again:
“For one with a lofty mind, who is heedful,
a sage training in the paths of sagehood—
sorrows do not arise for such a person.”
“For one who is always peaceful and mindful.

The bhikkhunīs said this: “Did we not say that today the exhortation will not be successful, and that now the venerable Cūḷapanthaka will simply repeat that same inspired utterance over and over again?
The venerable Cūḷapanthaka heard this conversation between those bhikkhunīs.
Then the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka rose up into the air and, in the sky, in the firmament, he walked back and forth, stood, sat down, and lay down;
he emitted smoke and burst into flames, and then vanished.
He uttered that very inspired utterance and much other word of the Buddha.
The bhikkhunīs said this:
“It is wonderful indeed, sir! It is marvelous indeed, sir!
Never before has the exhortation been so successful for us as it has been for the venerable Cūḷapanthaka.”
Then the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka, having exhorted those bhikkhunīs until darkness fell, dismissed them, saying, “Go, sisters.
Then those bhikkhunīs, having stayed outside the city because the city gates were closed, entered the city very early in the morning.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying, “These bhikkhunīs are unchaste;”
“Having stayed in the monastery together with the bhikkhus, they are now entering the city.
The bhikkhus heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
“How can the Venerable Cūḷapanthaka exhort the bhikkhunīs when the sun has set?
… [and so on] … “Is it true, Cūḷapanthaka, that you exhort the bhikkhunīs when the sun has set?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked him:
“… How can you, Cūḷapanthaka, exhort the bhikkhunīs after the sun has set?
This, Cūḷapanthaka, is neither for the inspiring of the faithless nor for the increase of the faithful…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:
“If a monk, even though he has been authorized, should exhort the bhikkhunīs after the sun has set, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Regarding the term “authorized”: [text continues].
He was appointed by a formal act consisting of a motion and three proclamations.
"When the sun has set" means when the sun has gone down.
"A bhikkhunī" means one who is fully ordained in both Saṅghas.
"Should exhort" means:
If she instructs her by means of the eight *garudhammas* or by any other rule, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If the sun has set and she perceives it as having set, and she instructs her, there is an offense of expiation.
If the sun has set and she is in doubt about it, and she instructs her, there is an offense of expiation.
If he instructs when the sun has set, perceiving that it has not set, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If he instructs one who is fully ordained on only one side, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If he instructs when the sun has not set, perceiving that it has set, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it has not yet set and he is in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it has not yet set and he perceives that it has not yet set, there is no offense.
There is no offense—
When giving a summary,
when giving a detailed questioning,
or when being told, "Recite, venerable lady," he recites.
She asks a question;
being asked a question, she speaks;
and while he is speaking for the sake of another, the bhikkhunīs listen.
for a trainee nun (sikkhamānā),
for a novice nun (sāmaṇerī),
for one who is insane (ummattaka).
"For one who is a first offender":
the second training rule concerning what has gone down is finished.
